decisions.choice: a short poem of lament over the fall of the proud (verses 1-3)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are a taunt in the form of a lament. The great trees of Lebanon and Bashan and the thickets of the Jordan are destroyed, and the shepherds wail. The poem links the promise of chapter 10, that the pride of the nations will be brought down (10:11), to the story of the shepherds that follows (11:4-17). It does not say which kingdom or which rulers it has in mind.

decisions.choice: Lebanon and its cedars: the proud and the powerful
decisions.reason: The cedars of Lebanon were the tallest and finest trees the Israelites knew, and they stand in the prophets for the pride of kings and nations (Isaiah 2:13; 10:33-34; Ezekiel 31:3-18). Jeremiah 22:6-7 uses them of the royal palace in Jerusalem. To "open your doors" to fire is to be left without defense.

decisions.choice: gates (B, R); cedar trees (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "doors" are the entrances to the land, its mountain passes; Balanced and Readable say "gates".

decisions.choice: junipers, the oaks of Bashan: the other great trees of the land
decisions.reason: The tree named first is a tall evergreen, a juniper or cypress, used with cedar for the finest buildings (1 Kings 5:22). Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for its oaks (Isaiah 2:13; Ezekiel 27:6). If even the cedar has fallen, the lesser trees have reason to wail.

decisions.choice: the impenetrable forest: following the reading tradition
alternatives: the forest of the vintage (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew can be read "the forest of the vintage", that is, the grape harvest. The reading tradition gives "the inaccessible forest", a forest too thick to enter, which fits the picture and is followed here.

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B); Cry out in grief (R); juniper
decisions.reason: "Wail" is "Cry out in grief" at Readable, as in Isaiah, and the tree is a juniper, as in Isaiah 14:8.

decisions.choice: "Gime" (singular) ... "{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Hebrew: the juniper is addressed in the singular, the oaks of Bashan in the plural, which takes the plural_you setting. Balanced and Readable address the junipers in the plural, as the English does.

ko.L: 목자들이 울부짖는 소리가 [들린다]. \q 그들의 영광이 망하였기 때문이다. \q 젊은 사자들이 포효하는 소리가 [들린다]. \q 요단의 자랑이 망하였기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is destroyed: the rulers lament their loss
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 25:34-36 hears the same cry: "Wail, you shepherds ... for the LORD is destroying their pasture." The shepherds stand for the rulers (10:3). Their "glory" is the richness of their pastures, the source of their wealth; the same word is used of a fine cloak in 13:4.

decisions.choice: the young lions; the pride of the Jordan: the thick growth along the river where lions lived
decisions.reason: The Jordan valley was lined with dense thickets where lions made their dens (Jeremiah 12:5; 49:19). When the thickets are destroyed, the lions roar for the loss of their home. The lions, like the shepherds, may stand for rulers (Ezekiel 19:1-9).

decisions.choice: [Listen to] (L); Listen to (B, R); the thickets of the Jordan (B); the thick bushes along the Jordan River (R); their rich pastures (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins each half with "the sound of", a cry calling for attention (Isaiah 40:3); Literal brackets "Listen to", and Balanced ("Hear") and Readable ("Listen to") give it as a command. Balanced and Readable say what "the pride of the Jordan" was, and Readable what the shepherds' glory was (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "[Se oye]" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies an impersonal verb for "the sound of", so the bracket needs no plural_you span; Balanced and Readable give it as a command to the hearers, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "소리가 [들린다]" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot leave "the sound of" without a verb; Literal supplies the plainest one, and Balanced and Readable say "들어라", "들어 보아라" as the English does.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD my God: the prophet tells, in prose, of a part he was told to act
decisions.reason: From here to verse 16 the prophet tells in the first person how the LORD told him to act the part of a shepherd, and what happened. Like Hosea's marriage (Hosea 1-3) or Jeremiah's loincloth (Jeremiah 13:1-11), the actions are a message. The passage is among the hardest in the prophets: the flock, its buyers and sellers, the three shepherds and the staffs are not explained, and readers have identified them in very different ways. The translation keeps to what the text says.

decisions.choice: the flock for slaughter: a flock raised only to be killed
decisions.reason: Sheep raised for slaughter were bought and sold for their meat; no one cared for them for their own sake. The people are like such a flock, exploited by those who should protect them (Psalm 44:23; Jeremiah 12:3). Verse 5 says who these exploiters are.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD my God (L); The LORD my God says this (B); This is what the LORD my God says (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in Isaiah, with "my God" added as in the Hebrew. In this prose story the LORD's words are quoted with quotation marks, as in Jeremiah 13:1. Literal and Balanced end with a comma, because the sentence goes on into verse 5; Literal brackets "doomed".

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời của tôi"; God's command with no pronoun
decisions.reason: The prophet tells this story in his own voice (meaning decision m1), so he says "tôi"; God's commands to him need no pronoun here, and where one is needed it is "ngươi" (L) / "con" (B, R), as the terms note sets for God speaking to a prophet.

decisions.choice: the sentence closes at the end of verse 4 (L, B)
decisions.reason: Korean puts a relative clause before its noun, so verse 5's description of the flock cannot follow it as in the Hebrew; each verse is closed as its own sentence and verse 5 names the flock again.

es.L: cuyos compradores lo matan y no son tenidos por culpables; y los que lo venden dicen: “Bendito [sea] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, porque me he enriquecido”; y sus propios pastores no tienen compasión de él.
es.B: cuyos compradores lo degüellan y quedan sin castigo. Los que lo venden dicen: “¡Alabado sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, soy rico!”. Y sus propios pastores no le tienen lástima.
es.R: Los que las compran las matan y no reciben castigo. Los que las venden dicen: “¡Alabado sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! ¡Ahora soy rico!”. Ni siquiera sus propios pastores sienten lástima por ellas.

fr.L: dont les acheteurs les tuent sans être tenus pour coupables ; et ceux qui les vendent disent : “Béni [soit] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car je me suis enrichi !” et leurs propres bergers n’ont pas de compassion pour elles.
fr.B: dont les acheteurs les égorgent sans être punis. Ceux qui les vendent disent : “Loué soit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je suis riche !” Et leurs propres bergers n’ont aucune pitié d’elles.
fr.R: Ceux qui les achètent les tuent et ne sont pas punis. Ceux qui les vendent disent : “Loué soit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Me voilà riche !” Même leurs propres bergers n’ont pas pitié d’eux.

sw.L: ambao wanunuzi wao huwaua na hawahesabiwi kuwa na hatia; na wauzaji wao husema, 'Na ahimidiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana nimetajirika!' na wachungaji wao wenyewe hawawahurumii.
sw.B: ambao wanunuzi wao huwachinja bila kuadhibiwa. Wauzaji wao husema, 'Asifiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nimetajirika!' Na wachungaji wao wenyewe hawawaonei huruma.
sw.R: Wale wanaowanunua huwaua na hawaadhibiwi. Wale wanaowauza husema, 'Asifiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Sasa nimekuwa tajiri!' Hata wachungaji wao wenyewe hawawahurumii.

vi.L: là bầy mà những kẻ mua giết chúng mà không bị kể là có tội; còn những kẻ bán chúng thì nói: 'Chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì tôi đã trở nên giàu có!' và chính những người chăn của chúng cũng không thương xót chúng.
vi.B: là bầy mà kẻ mua giết thịt chúng mà không bị trừng phạt. Những kẻ bán chúng nói: 'Ngợi khen {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi giàu rồi!' Và chính những người chăn của chúng cũng chẳng thương hại chúng.
vi.R: Những kẻ mua chúng giết chúng mà không bị phạt. Những kẻ bán chúng nói: 'Ngợi khen {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Bây giờ tôi giàu rồi!' Ngay cả những người chăn của chúng cũng không thương xót chúng.

ko.L: 그 양 떼를 산 자들은 그것들을 죽이고도 죄가 없다 여기고, 그것들을 판 자들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 찬송을 받으실 분이다. 내가 부유하게 되었다!' 하고 말하며, 그것들의 목자들도 그것들을 불쌍히 여기지 않는다.
ko.B: 그 양들을 산 자들은 양들을 잡아도 벌을 받지 않는다. 그것들을 판 자들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 찬양을! 내가 부자가 되었다!' 하고 말한다. 그 양들의 목자들조차 그것들을 불쌍히 여기지 않는다.
ko.R: 양들을 사는 사람들은 그것들을 잡아 죽여도 벌을 받지 않는다. 양들을 파는 사람들은 '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하자! 이제 나는 부자가 되었다!' 하고 말한다. 양들의 목자들마저 그것들을 불쌍히 여기지 않는다.

decisions.choice: buyers, sellers and shepherds: those who profit from the flock
decisions.reason: The buyers kill the sheep for meat, the sellers grow rich from the sale, and the shepherds who should care for them do nothing. The picture is of rulers, foreign and native, who used the people for their own gain (Ezekiel 34:2-6). The text does not say who they were.

decisions.choice: are not held guilty: they suffer no punishment and feel no guilt
decisions.reason: The verb means to be guilty or to bear the penalty for guilt. The buyers act as though harming this flock carried no blame (Jeremiah 2:3; 50:7).

decisions.choice: Blessed be the LORD, for I have become rich: greed in the language of piety
decisions.reason: The seller thanks God for his profit, made from the flock's destruction. Hosea 12:9 hears the same boast from a cheating merchant. The words are a bitter irony.

decisions.choice: go unpunished (B); are not punished (R); Praise the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Praise the LORD" for the blessing formula, as English speakers thank God. The words of the sellers are quoted within the LORD's words, so they take single quotation marks.

source.text: כִּ֠י לֹ֣א אֶחְמ֥וֹל ע֛וֹד עַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַמְצִ֣יא אֶת־הָאָדָ֗ם אִ֤ישׁ בְּיַד־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ וּבְיַ֣ד מַלְכּ֔וֹ וְכִתְּתוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א אַצִּ֖יל מִיָּדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For I will not have compassion again on [the] inhabitants of the land, declaration of Yahweh; and look, I [am] delivering the humankind, each into [the] hand of his neighbor and into [the] hand of his king; and they will crush the land, and I will not deliver from their hand.

en.L: For I will no longer have compassion on the inhabitants of the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And look, I am handing over every person, each into the hand of {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and into the hand of {{gender:their|his}} king; and they will crush the land, and I will not rescue [it] from their hand."
en.B: For I will no longer pity the people who live in the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am about to hand everyone over to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and to {{gender:their|his}} king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their power."
en.R: I will no longer feel sorry for the people who live in the land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am going to let the people fall into the power of their neighbors and their king. They will destroy the land, and I will not rescue anyone from them."

es.L: Porque ya no tendré compasión de los habitantes de la tierra, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Y he aquí, yo entrego a todo ser humano, a cada uno en mano de su prójimo y en mano de su rey; y ellos aplastarán la tierra, y no [la] libraré de su mano».
es.B: Porque ya no tendré lástima de los que habitan en la tierra, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Voy a entregar a cada uno en manos de su prójimo y de su rey. Ellos aplastarán la tierra, y yo no libraré a nadie de su poder».
es.R: Ya no sentiré lástima por la gente que vive en la tierra, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Voy a dejar que caigan en manos de sus vecinos y de su rey. Ellos destruirán la tierra, y yo no rescataré a nadie de sus manos».

fr.L: Car je n’aurai plus compassion des habitants du pays, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et voici, je livre les humains, chacun aux mains de son prochain et aux mains de son roi ; et ils écraseront le pays, et je ne [le] délivrerai pas de leur main. »
fr.B: Car je n’aurai plus pitié des habitants du pays, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je vais livrer chacun aux mains de son prochain et aux mains de son roi. Ils écraseront le pays, et je ne délivrerai personne de leur pouvoir. »
fr.R: Je n’aurai plus pitié des gens qui habitent le pays, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je vais laisser les gens tomber au pouvoir de leurs voisins et de leur roi. Ils détruiront le pays, et je ne sauverai personne de leurs mains. »

sw.L: Kwa maana sitawahurumia tena wakaaji wa nchi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Na tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninawatia wanadamu, kila mtu mkononi mwa jirani yake na mkononi mwa mfalme wake; nao wataiponda nchi, wala sitaiokoa [nchi] mkononi mwao."
sw.B: Kwa maana sitawahurumia tena watu wanaoishi katika nchi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitamtia kila mtu mikononi mwa jirani yake na mikononi mwa mfalme wake. Wataiponda nchi, wala sitamwokoa mtu yeyote kutoka mikononi mwao."
sw.R: Sitawahurumia tena watu wanaoishi katika nchi, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitawaacha watu waanguke katika mamlaka ya jirani zao na ya mfalme wao. Wataiharibu nchi, wala sitamwokoa mtu yeyote kutoka kwao."

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không còn thương xót dân cư trong xứ nữa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Và kìa, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó loài người, mỗi người vào tay kẻ lân cận mình và vào tay vua mình; chúng sẽ chà nát xứ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không giải cứu [xứ] khỏi tay chúng."
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không còn thương hại dân cư trong xứ nữa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Ta sẽ phó mỗi người vào tay kẻ lân cận mình và vào tay vua mình. Chúng sẽ chà nát xứ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không giải cứu ai khỏi quyền lực của chúng."
vi.R: Ta sẽ không còn thương xót những người sống trong xứ nữa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ta sẽ để dân chúng rơi vào quyền lực của những người láng giềng và của vua họ. Chúng sẽ tàn phá xứ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không giải cứu ai khỏi tay chúng."

ko.L: 내가 다시는 그 땅 주민들을 불쌍히 여기지 않을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 보아라, 내가 사람들을 각각 그 이웃의 손과 그 왕의 손에 넘겨주겠다. 그들이 그 땅을 짓밟을 것이나, 내가 [그 땅을] 그들의 손에서 건져 내지 않겠다."
ko.B: 나는 다시는 이 땅에 사는 사람들을 불쌍히 여기지 않겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 모든 사람을 각자의 이웃과 왕의 손에 넘기겠다. 그들이 이 땅을 짓밟아도, 나는 아무도 그들의 손에서 구해 주지 않겠다."
ko.R: 나는 더 이상 이 땅에 사는 사람들을 불쌍히 여기지 않겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 사람들을 그들의 이웃과 왕의 손에 넘기겠다. 그들이 이 땅을 망가뜨려도, 나는 아무도 그들에게서 구해 주지 않겠다."

decisions.choice: I will no longer have compassion: the LORD hands the people over to judgment
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the shepherds' lack of compassion (verse 5) with the same verb: he too will no longer spare the people. The "inhabitants of the land" are most likely the people of Israel. The LORD gives them over to their own neighbors and rulers, and does not rescue them, a judgment like the one Jeremiah spoke (Jeremiah 13:14; 21:7).

decisions.choice: each into the hand of their neighbor and their king: civil strife and harsh rule
decisions.reason: The people will turn on one another, and their king will oppress them. "His king" may be the people's own ruler or a foreign one. To be "in the hand" of someone is to be in their power.

decisions.choice: each into the hand of their neighbor (L, B); their (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "each ... his" means everyone, men and women, so Literal and Balanced take the gender setting. Readable speaks of "the people" in the plural and needs no setting. "Declares the LORD" follows the wording set in Isaiah, and the LORD's words, quoted since verse 4, end here.

decisions.choice: "a cada uno en mano de su prójimo", with no gender span
alternatives: "a cada persona en mano de su prójimo"
decisions.reason: Spanish "cada uno" and "su" already include men and women, so the English gender span has nothing to change in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "chacun aux mains de son prochain", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Chacun" and "son" are already generic in French; where the English needs a span only for a pronoun, French adds none (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "kila mtu ... jirani yake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" and "-ake" already cover both sexes, so Swahili needs no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: "mỗi người ... kẻ lân cận mình", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Người" and "mình" are already inclusive, so Vietnamese needs no gender span here.

decisions.choice: "각각 그 이웃", "각자의 이웃", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean uses no pronoun here, and "사람", "각자" already include men and women.

source.text: וָֽאֶרְעֶה֙ אֶת־צֹ֣אן הַֽהֲרֵגָ֔ה לָכֵ֖ן עֲנִיֵּ֣י הַצֹּ֑אן וָאֶקַּֽח־לִ֞י שְׁנֵ֣י מַקְל֗וֹת לְאַחַ֞ד קָרָ֤אתִי נֹ֨עַם֙ וּלְאַחַד֙ קָרָ֣אתִי חֹֽבְלִ֔ים וָאֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶת־הַצֹּֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I shepherded the flock of the slaughter, therefore the afflicted of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs; one I called Favor, and one I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.

en.L: So I shepherded the flock [doomed] for slaughter, truly the afflicted of the flock. And I took for myself two staffs: one I called Favor, and one I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
en.B: So I became shepherd of the flock marked for slaughter, the most afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs; one I named Favor and the other Union, and I shepherded the flock.
en.R: So I took care of the sheep that were going to be slaughtered, the sheep that were suffering most. I took two shepherd's staffs. I named one of them Favor and the other Union. Then I took care of the sheep.

es.L: Y apacenté el rebaño [destinado] a la matanza, en verdad a los afligidos del rebaño. Y tomé para mí dos cayados: a uno llamé Favor, y a otro llamé Unión; y apacenté el rebaño.
es.B: Así que me hice pastor del rebaño marcado para la matanza, los más afligidos del rebaño. Tomé dos cayados; a uno lo llamé Favor y al otro Unión, y apacenté el rebaño.
es.R: Así que cuidé de las ovejas que iban a ser sacrificadas, las ovejas que más sufrían. Tomé dos cayados de pastor. A uno le puse por nombre Favor y al otro Unión. Luego cuidé de las ovejas.

fr.L: Et je fis paître les brebis [destinées] à la boucherie, vraiment les malheureuses du troupeau. Et je pris pour moi deux bâtons : l’un, je l’appelai Faveur, et l’autre, je l’appelai Union ; et je fis paître le troupeau.
fr.B: Je devins donc le berger des brebis vouées à l’abattoir, les plus malheureuses du troupeau. Je pris deux bâtons ; je nommai l’un Faveur et l’autre Union, et je fis paître le troupeau.
fr.R: Alors j’ai pris soin des moutons qui allaient être abattus, les moutons qui souffraient le plus. J’ai pris deux bâtons de berger. J’ai appelé l’un Faveur et l’autre Union. Puis j’ai pris soin des moutons.

sw.L: Basi nililichunga kundi [lililowekwa] kwa machinjo, kweli wanyonge wa kundi. Nikajitwalia fimbo mbili: moja nikaiita Neema, na nyingine nikaiita Umoja; nikalichunga kundi.
sw.B: Basi nikawa mchungaji wa kundi lililotengwa kwa ajili ya kuchinjwa, wale walioteseka zaidi katika kundi. Nilichukua fimbo mbili; moja nikaiita Neema na nyingine Umoja, nikalichunga kundi.
sw.R: Basi niliwatunza kondoo waliokuwa watachinjwa, kondoo walioteseka kuliko wote. Nilichukua fimbo mbili za mchungaji. Moja niliiita Neema na nyingine Umoja. Kisha nikawatunza kondoo.

vi.L: Vậy tôi chăn bầy chiên [bị định] cho sự tàn sát, thật là những con khốn khổ của bầy. Tôi lấy cho mình hai cây gậy: một cây tôi gọi là Ân Huệ, một cây tôi gọi là Hiệp Nhất; và tôi chăn bầy chiên.
vi.B: Vậy tôi làm người chăn bầy chiên đã bị định cho lò sát sinh, là những con khốn khổ nhất trong bầy. Tôi lấy hai cây gậy; một cây tôi đặt tên là Ân Huệ, cây kia là Hiệp Nhất, và tôi chăn bầy chiên.
vi.R: Vậy tôi chăm sóc bầy chiên sắp bị giết thịt, là những con chiên khổ sở nhất. Tôi lấy hai cây gậy chăn chiên. Tôi đặt tên một cây là Ân Huệ và cây kia là Hiệp Nhất. Rồi tôi chăm sóc bầy chiên.

ko.L: 그리하여 내가 도살당할 양 떼, 곧 양 떼 가운데 괴로움 당하는 것들을 쳤다. 내가 나를 위하여 지팡이 둘을 가져다가, 하나는 '은총'이라 부르고, 하나는 '연합'이라 불렀다. 그리고 내가 양 떼를 쳤다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 도살당하기로 정해진 양 떼, 곧 양 떼 가운데 가장 괴로움을 당하는 것들의 목자가 되었다. 나는 지팡이 둘을 가져다가 하나는 '은총', 다른 하나는 '연합'이라고 이름 짓고, 양 떼를 쳤다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 곧 잡혀 죽을 양들, 가장 고통받는 양들을 돌보았다. 나는 목자의 지팡이 두 개를 가져다가, 하나는 '은총', 다른 하나는 '연합'이라고 이름을 붙였다. 그리고 그 양들을 돌보았다.

decisions.choice: truly the afflicted of the flock: following the Hebrew text
alternatives: for the sheep traders (following the Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "therefore (or "truly") the afflicted of the flock". The Septuagint read the same letters as one word, "for the Canaanites", that is, the traders, giving "the flock doomed to slaughter for the sheep traders". The same choice comes again in verse 11. Many modern translations follow the Greek. The Hebrew text is kept here; it speaks of the poor of the flock, whom the shepherd cares for.

decisions.choice: Favor and Union: the names of the two staffs
decisions.reason: A shepherd carried a staff to guide and guard the flock (Psalm 23:4). The first name means pleasantness, grace or favor: the LORD's kindness that protects the flock (Psalm 90:17 uses the word). The second means "bonds" or "cords", the ties that bind the people together. Verses 10 and 14 explain the names when the staffs are broken.

decisions.choice: Favor, Union (every level)
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level, because the story turns on what they mean (m2). Readable says "shepherd's staffs".

decisions.choice: "Favor" and "Unión" for the staffs
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level, as in the English (meaning decision m2); "Unión" keeps the sense of bonds that hold the people together, which verse 14 explains.

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R) for the prophet's story (11:7-17)
decisions.reason: The prophet tells in the first person what he did, as in the night visions, so it is narrative: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable. "Faveur" and "Union" translate the staffs' names at every level (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "Neema" and "Umoja" for the staffs
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level (meaning decision m2): "Neema" for the LORD's favor and "Umoja" for the bonds that hold the people together (verse 14).

decisions.choice: "Ân Huệ" and "Hiệp Nhất" for the staffs
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level (meaning decision m2), capitalised as names: "Ân Huệ" for favor and "Hiệp Nhất" for the bond of unity that verse 14 explains.

decisions.choice: "'은총'" and "'연합'" for the staffs, in single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The names are translated at every level (meaning decision m2) and set in quotation marks so they read as names, as Hosea's translated names are.

source.text: וָאַכְחִ֛ד אֶת־שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָרֹעִ֖ים בְּיֶ֣רַח אֶחָ֑ד וַתִּקְצַ֤ר נַפְשִׁי֙ בָּהֶ֔ם וְגַם־נַפְשָׁ֖ם בָּחֲלָ֥ה בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I destroyed the three shepherds in one month; and my soul was short with them, and also their soul loathed me.

en.L: And I wiped out the three shepherds in one month. And my soul was impatient with them, and their soul also loathed me.
en.B: In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. Then I lost patience with the flock, and they, for their part, loathed me.
en.R: In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. Then I grew tired of the sheep, and they hated me.

es.L: Y eliminé a los tres pastores en un mes. Y mi alma se impacientó con ellos, y también el alma de ellos me aborreció.
es.B: En un mes me deshice de los tres pastores. Entonces perdí la paciencia con el rebaño, y ellos, por su parte, me aborrecieron.
es.R: En un mes me deshice de los tres pastores. Después me cansé de las ovejas, y ellas me odiaron.

fr.L: Et je fis disparaître les trois bergers en un mois. Et mon âme perdit patience avec eux, et leur âme aussi me prit en dégoût.
fr.B: En un mois, je me débarrassai des trois bergers. Puis je perdis patience avec le troupeau, et lui, de son côté, me prit en dégoût.
fr.R: En un mois, je me suis débarrassé des trois bergers. Puis j’en ai eu assez des moutons, et ils m’ont détesté.

sw.L: Nikawaangamiza wachungaji watatu katika mwezi mmoja. Nafsi yangu ikakosa subira kwao, nayo nafsi yao pia ikanichukia.
sw.B: Katika mwezi mmoja niliwaondoa wale wachungaji watatu. Kisha nikakosa subira na kundi, nao kwa upande wao wakanichukia.
sw.R: Katika mwezi mmoja niliwaondoa wachungaji watatu. Kisha nikachoshwa na kondoo, nao wakanichukia.

vi.L: Tôi diệt ba người chăn trong một tháng. Linh hồn tôi mất kiên nhẫn với chúng, và linh hồn chúng cũng ghê tởm tôi.
vi.B: Trong một tháng, tôi loại bỏ ba người chăn. Rồi tôi mất kiên nhẫn với bầy chiên, còn chúng thì ghê tởm tôi.
vi.R: Trong một tháng, tôi loại bỏ ba người chăn. Rồi tôi chán ngán bầy chiên, và chúng cũng ghét tôi.

ko.L: 내가 한 달 안에 세 목자를 없애 버렸다. 내 영혼이 그들을 참지 못하였고, 그들의 영혼도 나를 싫어하였다.
ko.B: 나는 한 달 안에 세 목자를 없앴다. 그러자 나는 양 떼를 더 이상 참을 수 없었고, 양 떼도 나를 싫어하였다.
ko.R: 나는 한 달 안에 세 목자를 쫓아냈다. 그 뒤에 나는 양들에게 지쳤고, 양들도 나를 미워했다.

decisions.choice: the three shepherds in one month: rulers removed quickly, who they were is unknown
decisions.reason: The text does not say who the three shepherds were. Readers have suggested kings of Israel who reigned briefly (2 Kings 15:8-15), high priests, foreign rulers, or the three offices of king, priest and prophet; more than forty identifications have been offered. The point that is clear is that the shepherd removed the bad rulers quickly, within one month.

decisions.choice: impatient with them ... they loathed me: the flock and the shepherd turn against each other
decisions.reason: "Them" most likely means the flock, which the shepherd addresses in the next verse; it may also mean the three shepherds. The relationship between the shepherd and the people breaks down from both sides.

decisions.choice: with the flock (B); of the sheep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are (m2). Literal keeps "my soul was impatient", "their soul ... loathed", the Hebrew way of saying "I" and "they".

source.text: וָאֹמַ֕ר לֹ֥א אֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם הַמֵּתָ֣ה תָמ֗וּת וְהַנִּכְחֶ֨דֶת֙ תִּכָּחֵ֔ד וְהַ֨נִּשְׁאָר֔וֹת תֹּאכַ֕לְנָה אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־בְּשַׂ֥ר רְעוּתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said, I will not shepherd you; the dying let die, and the being destroyed let be destroyed, and those left let devour each the flesh of her neighbor.

en.L: And I said, "I will not shepherd you. What is dying, let it die; and what is being destroyed, let it be destroyed; and those that are left, let them devour one another's flesh."
en.B: Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die and the perishing perish, and let those that are left eat one another's flesh."
en.R: Then I said to the sheep, "I will not take care of you any longer. Let the ones that are dying die. Let the ones that are being destroyed be destroyed. Let the ones that are left eat each other's flesh."

es.L: Y dije: «No {{plural_you:las|os}} apacentaré. La que muere, que muera; y la que se pierde, que se pierda; y las que queden, que se coman cada una la carne de su compañera».
es.B: Entonces dije: «No seré {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} pastor. Que muera la que se está muriendo y que perezca la que perece, y que las que queden se coman la carne unas de otras».
es.R: Entonces les dije a las ovejas: «Ya no {{plural_you:las|os}} cuidaré. Que mueran las que se están muriendo. Que sean destruidas las que están siendo destruidas. Que las que queden se coman unas a otras».

fr.L: Et je dis : « Je ne vous ferai pas paître. Celle qui meurt, qu’elle meure ; et celle qui périt, qu’elle périsse ; et celles qui restent, qu’elles dévorent chacune la chair de sa voisine. »
fr.B: Puis je dis : « Je ne serai pas votre berger. Que la mourante meure et que celle qui périt périsse, et que celles qui restent se dévorent la chair les unes des autres ! »
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit aux moutons : « Je ne prendrai plus soin de vous. Que ceux qui sont en train de mourir meurent. Que ceux qui sont en train de périr périssent. Que ceux qui restent se mangent les uns les autres ! »

sw.L: Nikasema, "Sitawachunga ninyi. Anayekufa na afe; na anayeangamia na aangamie; na wanaobaki na walane kila mmoja nyama ya mwenzake."
sw.B: Kisha nikasema, "Sitakuwa mchungaji wenu. Anayekufa na afe, na anayeangamia na aangamie, na wale wanaobaki walane nyama wao kwa wao."
sw.R: Kisha nikawaambia kondoo, "Sitawatunza tena. Wanaokufa na wafe. Wanaoangamizwa na waangamizwe. Wanaobaki na walane nyama wao kwa wao."

vi.L: Tôi nói: "Tôi sẽ không chăn các ngươi. Con nào chết, cứ để nó chết; con nào bị diệt, cứ để nó bị diệt; còn những con sót lại, cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."
vi.B: Rồi tôi nói: "Tôi sẽ không làm người chăn của các ngươi. Con nào sắp chết cứ để nó chết, con nào sắp bị diệt cứ để nó bị diệt, và những con còn lại cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."
vi.R: Rồi tôi nói với bầy chiên: "Tôi sẽ không chăm sóc các ngươi nữa. Con nào đang chết, cứ để nó chết. Con nào đang bị diệt, cứ để nó bị diệt. Những con còn lại, cứ để chúng ăn thịt lẫn nhau."

ko.L: 내가 말하였다. "내가 너희를 치지 않겠다. 죽어 가는 것은 죽어라. 망해 가는 것은 망해라. 남은 것들은 저마다 이웃의 살을 먹어라."
ko.B: 그리고 내가 말하였다. "나는 너희의 목자가 되지 않겠다. 죽을 것은 죽고 망할 것은 망하여라. 남은 것들은 서로 살을 뜯어 먹어라."
ko.R: 그리고 나는 양들에게 말했다. "나는 이제 더 이상 너희를 돌보지 않겠다. 죽어 가는 것은 죽어라. 망해 가는 것은 망해라. 남은 것들은 서로 잡아먹어라."

decisions.choice: the dying, the being destroyed, those that are left: the sheep are given up to their fate
decisions.reason: The forms are feminine, for the ewes of the flock. The shepherd no longer protects them from death, from destruction or from one another. Ezekiel 34:4 blames the shepherds for leaving the weak to perish; here the shepherd does so as a judgment.

decisions.choice: devour one another's flesh: the people turn on one another
decisions.reason: Sheep do not eat each other; the picture is of a people destroying itself through strife or the horror of famine in a siege (Isaiah 9:19; Jeremiah 19:9).

decisions.choice: said to the sheep; any longer (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the sheep as the ones addressed and breaks the list into short sentences.

decisions.choice: feminine forms: "la que muere", "las que queden", "{{plural_you:las|os}}"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew forms are feminine, for the ewes of the flock (meaning decision m1); Spanish "ovejas" can keep them.

decisions.choice: feminine forms: "celle qui meurt", "celles qui restent" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew forms are feminine, for the ewes (meaning decision m1), which French "brebis" keeps; Readable says "moutons", as the terms note sets for that level.

source.text: וָאֶקַּ֤ח אֶת־מַקְלִי֙ אֶת־נֹ֔עַם וָאֶגְדַּ֖ע אֹת֑וֹ לְהָפֵיר֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת־כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I took my staff Favor and cut it in pieces, to break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.

en.L: And I took my staff Favor and cut it in pieces, to break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
en.B: Then I took my staff named Favor and broke it, to annul the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
en.R: Then I took the staff I had named Favor and broke it in pieces. This showed that I was canceling the agreement I had made with all the nations.

es.L: Y tomé mi cayado Favor y lo hice pedazos, para romper mi pacto que había hecho con todos los pueblos.
es.B: Luego tomé mi cayado llamado Favor y lo quebré, para anular el pacto que había hecho con todos los pueblos.
es.R: Luego tomé el cayado al que había puesto por nombre Favor y lo hice pedazos. Así mostré que cancelaba el acuerdo que había hecho con todas las naciones.

fr.L: Et je pris mon bâton Faveur et je le mis en pièces, pour rompre mon alliance que j’avais conclue avec tous les peuples.
fr.B: Puis je pris mon bâton nommé Faveur et je le brisai, pour annuler l’alliance que j’avais conclue avec tous les peuples.
fr.R: Puis j’ai pris le bâton que j’avais appelé Faveur et je l’ai cassé en morceaux. Cela montrait que j’annulais l’accord que j’avais fait avec toutes les nations.

sw.L: Nikaichukua fimbo yangu Neema, nikaikata vipande vipande, ili kulivunja agano langu nililofanya na mataifa yote.
sw.B: Kisha nikaichukua fimbo yangu iitwayo Neema, nikaivunja, ili kulitangua agano nililofanya na mataifa yote.
sw.R: Kisha nikaichukua ile fimbo niliyoiita Neema, nikaivunja vipande vipande. Hii ilionyesha kwamba nilikuwa ninayavunja mapatano niliyofanya na mataifa yote.

vi.L: Tôi lấy cây gậy Ân Huệ của tôi và chặt nó ra từng khúc, để hủy bỏ giao ước của tôi đã lập với tất cả các dân.
vi.B: Rồi tôi lấy cây gậy tên là Ân Huệ mà bẻ gãy, để hủy giao ước tôi đã lập với tất cả các dân.
vi.R: Rồi tôi lấy cây gậy mà tôi đã đặt tên là Ân Huệ và bẻ nó ra từng khúc. Việc đó cho thấy tôi hủy bỏ thỏa ước tôi đã lập với mọi dân tộc.

ko.L: 내가 내 지팡이 '은총'을 가져다가 그것을 산산이 꺾었다. 내가 모든 민족과 맺은 내 언약을 깨뜨리려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 나는 '은총'이라는 내 지팡이를 가져다가 꺾었다. 내가 모든 민족과 맺은 언약을 깨뜨리려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 나는 '은총'이라고 이름 붙인 지팡이를 가져다가 산산이 꺾었다. 그것은 내가 모든 민족과 맺은 약속을 깨뜨린다는 뜻이었다.

decisions.choice: my covenant with all the peoples: the protection that kept the nations back is withdrawn
decisions.reason: The covenant is not explained. It is most likely an agreement that kept the nations from harming the flock, like the covenant with the wild animals in Hosea 2:20 and Ezekiel 34:25. When Favor is broken, that protection ends. The prophet speaks as the shepherd, but the covenant is the LORD's to give and to take away: the people recognize "the word of the LORD" in it (verse 11).

decisions.choice: my staff, my covenant: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The speaker is the prophet acting the part of the shepherd, so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun span, even where he acts for the LORD (m1). Readable says "agreement" for "covenant" and "nations" for "peoples".

decisions.choice: the purpose clause as a second sentence (L, B)
decisions.reason: Korean would put the purpose before the action; a second sentence keeps the Hebrew order of taking, breaking and then the meaning of the act.

source.text: וַתֻּפַ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֵּדְע֨וּ כֵ֜ן עֲנִיֵּ֤י הַצֹּאן֙ הַשֹּׁמְרִ֣ים אֹתִ֔י כִּ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was broken on that day, and so knew the afflicted of the flock who were watching me that [it was the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: And it was broken on that day, and thus the afflicted of the flock, the ones watching me, knew that it [was] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s word.
en.B: It was broken on that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me understood that this was a word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So it was canceled that day. The suffering sheep that were watching me knew that this was a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y fue roto en aquel día, y así conocieron los afligidos del rebaño, los que me observaban, que [era] palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Fue anulado aquel día, y los afligidos del rebaño que me observaban comprendieron que aquello era palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Así que el acuerdo quedó cancelado ese día. Las ovejas que sufrían y que me estaban mirando supieron que aquello era un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et elle fut rompue en ce jour-là, et ainsi les malheureuses du troupeau, celles qui m’observaient, surent que c’[était] la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Elle fut rompue ce jour-là, et les malheureuses du troupeau qui m’observaient comprirent que c’était une parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: L’accord a donc été annulé ce jour-là. Les moutons qui souffraient et qui me regardaient ont su que c’était un message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Likavunjwa siku hiyo, na hivyo wanyonge wa kundi, wale walionitazama, wakajua kwamba [hilo lilikuwa] neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Lilivunjwa siku hiyo, na wanyonge wa kundi waliokuwa wakinitazama wakatambua kwamba hilo lilikuwa neno kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Basi mapatano hayo yakavunjwa siku hiyo. Kondoo walioteseka waliokuwa wakinitazama walijua kwamba huo ulikuwa ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Nó bị hủy bỏ trong ngày đó, và vì thế những con khốn khổ của bầy, là những con đang dõi theo tôi, biết rằng đó [là] lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Giao ước bị hủy bỏ trong ngày đó, và những con khốn khổ trong bầy đang dõi theo tôi hiểu rằng đây là lời từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Vậy giao ước bị hủy ngay ngày đó. Những con chiên khổ sở đang nhìn tôi biết rằng đó là sứ điệp từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그날에 그것이 깨어졌다. 그리하여 나를 지켜보던 양 떼 가운데 괴로움 당하는 것들이, 그것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀[이었음]을 알았다.
ko.B: 그 언약은 그날 깨어졌다. 나를 지켜보던, 양 떼 가운데 괴로움 당하는 것들은 그것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀임을 깨달았다.
ko.R: 그래서 그 약속은 그날 깨어졌다. 나를 지켜보던 고통받는 양들은 그것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 말씀임을 알았다.

decisions.choice: the afflicted of the flock: following the Hebrew text, as in verse 7
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, the Septuagint reads "the Canaanites", that is, the sheep traders, in place of "so the afflicted". Read that way, it is the traders who were watching and understood. The Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: who were watching me ... knew that it was the word of the LORD: the faithful few understood
decisions.reason: The poor of the flock watched what the shepherd did and saw in it a message from the LORD. A word from the LORD is shown to be true when it comes to pass (Deuteronomy 18:22; Jeremiah 32:8).

decisions.choice: on that day (every level)
decisions.reason: Here "on that day" refers to a day in the past, in the story, not to the coming day of the LORD, so it is not the prophetic formula of the Isaiah table, and every level says "on that day" (Readable "that day").

decisions.choice: "en aquel día" (L); "aquel día" (B); "ese día" (R)
decisions.reason: A day in the story, not the prophetic "in that day"; the Spanish happens to use the same words as the formula, since they are the plain way to say it.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אִם־ט֧וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֛ם הָב֥וּ שְׂכָרִ֖י וְאִם־לֹ֣א׀חֲדָ֑לוּ וַיִּשְׁקְל֥וּ אֶת־שְׂכָרִ֖י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to them, If [it is] good in your eyes, give my wages; and if not, refrain. And they weighed out my wages, thirty [of] silver.

en.L: And I said to them, "If [it is] good in your eyes, give [me] my wages; and if not, keep [them]." And they weighed out my wages, thirty [pieces of] silver.
en.B: Then I said to them, "If you think it right, give me my pay; but if not, keep it." So they weighed out my pay: thirty pieces of silver.
en.R: Then I said to them, "If you think it is right, pay me my wages. But if not, keep your money." So they weighed out thirty pieces of silver to pay me.

es.L: Y les dije: «Si [es] bueno a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos, {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} mi salario; y si no, {{plural_you:déjenlo|dejadlo}}». Y pesaron mi salario: treinta [piezas de] plata.
es.B: Entonces les dije: «Si {{plural_you:les|os}} parece bien, {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} mi paga; y si no, {{plural_you:guárdensela|guardáosla}}». Y me pesaron como paga treinta monedas de plata.
es.R: Entonces les dije: «Si {{plural_you:les|os}} parece justo, {{plural_you:páguenme|pagadme}} mi salario. Pero si no, {{plural_you:quédense con su dinero|quedaos con vuestro dinero}}». Así que me pesaron treinta monedas de plata como pago.

fr.L: Et je leur dis : « Si [c’est] bon à vos yeux, donnez[-moi] mon salaire ; et sinon, gardez[-le]. » Et ils pesèrent mon salaire : trente [pièces] d’argent.
fr.B: Puis je leur dis : « Si vous le jugez bon, donnez-moi mon salaire ; sinon, gardez-le. » Ils pesèrent alors mon salaire : trente pièces d’argent.
fr.R: Puis je leur ai dit : « Si vous pensez que c’est juste, payez-moi mon salaire. Sinon, gardez votre argent. » Alors ils ont pesé trente pièces d’argent pour me payer.

sw.L: Nikawaambia, "Ikiwa [ni] vema machoni penu, nipeni ujira wangu; na kama sivyo, acheni." Nao wakapima ujira wangu, [vipande] thelathini vya fedha.
sw.B: Kisha nikawaambia, "Mkiona ni haki, nipeni ujira wangu; lakini kama sivyo, bakini nao." Basi wakanipimia ujira wangu: vipande thelathini vya fedha.
sw.R: Kisha nikawaambia, "Mkiona ni sawa, nilipeni mshahara wangu. Lakini kama sivyo, bakini na fedha zenu." Basi wakanipimia sarafu thelathini za fedha kuwa malipo yangu.

vi.L: Tôi nói với họ: "Nếu các ông thấy [là] tốt, hãy trả tiền công cho tôi; còn nếu không, thì thôi." Và họ cân tiền công của tôi: ba mươi [đồng] bạc.
vi.B: Rồi tôi nói với họ: "Nếu các ông thấy phải, hãy trả công cho tôi; bằng không thì cứ giữ lại." Vậy họ cân tiền công cho tôi: ba mươi đồng bạc.

ko.R: 그래서 나는 그들에게 말했다. "여러분이 옳다고 생각하면 내 품삯을 주시오. 그렇지 않으면 그 돈은 그냥 가지고 있으시오." 그러자 그들은 은돈 서른 닢을 달아서 나에게 주었다.

decisions.choice: they weighed out thirty pieces of silver: the price of a slave
decisions.reason: Silver was weighed, not counted, before coins were common; the unit is the shekel, about two-fifths of an ounce. Thirty shekels was the payment the law set for a slave gored by an ox (Exodus 21:32). The wage was an insult: it valued the shepherd's work, and so the LORD's care for his people, at the price of a slave.

decisions.choice: to them: those who hired the shepherd
decisions.reason: The text does not say who "they" are: the sheep traders, the owners of the flock, or the leaders of the people. They are those for whom the shepherd worked and who now pay him off.

decisions.choice: thirty pieces of silver: Matthew 26:15 and 27:9
decisions.reason: In Matthew 26:15 the chief priests pay Judas thirty pieces of silver to betray Jesus, and Matthew 27:3-10 sees this passage fulfilled when the money is thrown into the temple and used to buy the potter's field (see verse 13).

decisions.choice: thirty [pieces of] silver (L); thirty pieces of silver (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "thirty silver"; every level names pieces of silver, as the reader knows them from Matthew, and Literal brackets the supplied words.

decisions.choice: "treinta [piezas de] plata" (L); "treinta monedas de plata" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the published Matthew 27:9 at each level, so the quotation can be seen (meaning decision m3), as the terms note asks.

decisions.choice: "trente [pièces] d'argent" (L); "trente pièces d'argent" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The key words of the published Matthew 26:15 and 27:9, so the quotation can be seen (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "vipande thelathini vya fedha" (L, B); "sarafu thelathini za fedha" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the published Matthew 27:9 at each level (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "các ông" to those who paid him; "ba mươi đồng bạc"
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to his employers in his own voice, plainly but not in rebuke, so he says "các ông". "Ba mươi đồng bạc" is the published Matthew 27:9.

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to me, Throw it to the potter, the magnificence of the price at which I was priced by them. And I took the thirty [of] silver and threw it [into the] house of Yahweh, to the potter.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw it to the potter, the magnificent price at which I was priced by them!" So I took the thirty [pieces of] silver and threw it [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the potter.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw it to the potter, that fine price they set on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!" Taking the thirty pieces of silver, I threw them into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the potter.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Throw the money to the potter. That is how little they think I am worth!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and threw them to the potter.

es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Échaselo al alfarero, ¡ese hermoso precio en que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} valoraron!». Tomé las treinta monedas de plata y las eché en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, al alfarero.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Échale el dinero al alfarero. ¡Así de poco creen que valgo!». Así que llevé las treinta monedas de plata al templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se las eché al alfarero.

fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Jette-le au potier, ce beau prix auquel ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont estimé ! » Je pris les trente pièces d’argent et je les jetai dans la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, au potier.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : « Jette l’argent au potier. Voilà le peu que je vaux à leurs yeux ! » J’ai donc pris les trente pièces d’argent, je les ai apportées au temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et je les ai jetées au potier.

vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với tôi: "Hãy ném số tiền ấy cho thợ gốm. Chúng coi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng đáng giá bao nhiêu!" Vậy tôi đem ba mươi đồng bạc đến đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và ném cho thợ gốm.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그것을 토기장이에게 던져라. 그들이 나를 평가한 그 훌륭한 값을!" 그래서 내가 은 서른 [닢]을 가져다가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에, 토기장이에게 던졌다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그들이 나에게 매긴 그 훌륭한 값을 토기장이에게 던져 버려라!" 나는 은돈 서른 닢을 가져다가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 토기장이에게 던졌다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 말씀하셨다. "그 돈을 그릇 만드는 사람에게 던져 버려라. 그들은 나를 그 정도밖에 안 되는 값으로 여긴다!" 그래서 나는 은돈 서른 닢을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전으로 가져가서 그릇 만드는 사람에게 던졌다.

decisions.choice: the magnificent price at which I was priced by them: said in scorn
decisions.reason: The LORD calls the thirty shekels a "magnificent price", in bitter irony. In the shepherd's wage the people had set a value on the LORD himself, and it was the price of a slave (verse 12). Here the LORD speaks of himself as the one priced.

decisions.choice: the potter: following the Hebrew text
alternatives: to the treasury (a change of one letter, as the Syriac reads)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the potter", both times. A potter may have worked for the temple, making vessels for its use, and throwing the money to him showed contempt for it, as something to be thrown away to a maker of cheap pots. The Syriac reads "to the treasury", which differs by one letter in Hebrew, and many readers follow it: the money was thrown into the temple treasury. The Hebrew text is kept here.

decisions.choice: quoted in Matthew 27:9-10, which names Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Matthew 27:9-10 sees this verse fulfilled when the chief priests take the thirty pieces of silver Judas threw into the temple and buy the potter's field. Matthew names the prophet Jeremiah. The words are closest to these verses, but Matthew joins them with themes from Jeremiah: the potter's house (Jeremiah 18:1-12), the potter's jar broken at the valley of slaughter (Jeremiah 19), and the field bought with silver (Jeremiah 32:6-15). The usual explanation is that he names the better-known prophet whose words also shape the quotation; some add that the scroll of the prophets was sometimes called by the name of Jeremiah, which stood first in it.

decisions.choice: the magnificent price at which I was priced (L); that fine price they set on me (B); how little they think I am worth (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the irony of the Hebrew (m1); Readable says plainly what it means. The LORD speaks of himself, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting at Balanced. Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD".

decisions.choice: "al alfarero" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text's "potter" (meaning decision m2), which is also the word of the published Matthew 27:10 ("el campo del alfarero").

decisions.choice: "au potier" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text's "potter" (meaning decision m2), the word of the published Matthew 27:10 ("le champ du potier").

decisions.choice: "mfinyanzi" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text's "potter" (meaning decision m2), as the published Matthew 27:10 ("shamba la mfinyanzi").

decisions.choice: "thợ gốm" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text's "potter" (meaning decision m2), as the published Matthew 27:10 ("ruộng của thợ gốm").

decisions.choice: "토기장이" (L, B); "그릇 만드는 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text's "potter" (meaning decision m2); Literal and Balanced keep the word of the published Matthew 27:10, and Readable uses the plain word the terms note sets for that level.

decisions.choice: to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel: the people's unity undone
decisions.reason: The staff named Union stood for the bonds that held the people together. Breaking it undoes the hope of a reunited people, which Ezekiel 37:15-22 pictured with two sticks joined into one in the prophet's hand, and which Zechariah 9:13 and 10:6 promised. The text does not say how the break came about.

decisions.choice: the one I had named Union; This showed that ... the family ties (R)
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader of the staff's name and says what breaking it meant, as in verse 10.

source.text: כִּ֣י הִנֵּֽה־אָנֹכִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים רֹעֶ֜ה בָּאָ֗רֶץ הַנִּכְחָד֤וֹת לֹֽא־יִפְקֹד֙ הַנַּ֣עַר לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּ֔שׁ וְהַנִּשְׁבֶּ֖רֶת לֹ֣א יְרַפֵּ֑א הַנִּצָּבָה֙ לֹ֣א יְכַלְכֵּ֔ל וּבְשַׂ֤ר הַבְּרִיאָה֙ יֹאכַ֔ל וּפַרְסֵיהֶ֖ן יְפָרֵֽק׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, I [am] raising up a shepherd in the land; the perishing he will not visit, the young he will not seek, and the broken he will not heal, the standing he will not sustain; and [the] flesh of the fat he will eat, and their hooves he will tear off.

en.L: For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land; the perishing he will not care for, the young he will not seek, and the broken he will not heal, the healthy he will not sustain; but the flesh of the fat he will eat, and their hooves he will tear off."
en.B: For I am about to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for the perishing, or look for the young, or heal the injured, or feed the healthy, but will eat the meat of the fat sheep and tear off their hooves."
en.R: I am going to give the land a shepherd who will not care about the sheep that are dying. He will not look for the young ones or heal the ones that are hurt. He will not feed the healthy ones. Instead, he will eat the meat of the fat sheep and even tear off their hooves."

es.L: Porque he aquí, yo levanto un pastor en la tierra; a la que perece no atenderá, a la joven no buscará, y a la quebrada no curará, a la sana no sostendrá; sino que la carne de las gordas comerá, y sus pezuñas arrancará».
es.B: Porque voy a levantar en la tierra un pastor que no cuidará de las que perecen, ni buscará a las pequeñas, ni curará a las heridas, ni alimentará a las sanas, sino que se comerá la carne de las ovejas gordas y les arrancará las pezuñas».
es.R: Voy a darle a la tierra un pastor que no se preocupará por las ovejas que se están muriendo. No buscará a las pequeñas ni curará a las que estén heridas. No alimentará a las sanas. Al contrario, se comerá la carne de las ovejas gordas y hasta les arrancará las pezuñas».

fr.L: Car voici, je suscite un berger dans le pays ; celles qui périssent, il ne s’en occupera pas, la jeune, il ne la cherchera pas, et la blessée, il ne la guérira pas, celle qui est saine, il ne la nourrira pas ; mais la chair des grasses, il la mangera, et leurs sabots, il les arrachera. »
fr.B: Car je vais susciter dans le pays un berger qui ne s’occupera pas de celles qui périssent, ne cherchera pas les jeunes, ne soignera pas les blessées et ne nourrira pas celles qui sont en bonne santé, mais qui mangera la chair des bêtes grasses et leur arrachera les sabots. »
fr.R: Je vais donner au pays un berger qui ne s’occupera pas des moutons qui sont en train de mourir. Il ne cherchera pas les jeunes et ne soignera pas ceux qui sont blessés. Il ne nourrira pas ceux qui sont en bonne santé. Au contraire, il mangera la viande des moutons gras et leur arrachera même les sabots. »

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninainua mchungaji katika nchi; wanaoangamia hatawajali, mchanga hatamtafuta, na aliyevunjika hatamponya, aliye mzima hatamlisha; lakini nyama ya walionona ataila, na kwato zao atazirarua."
sw.B: Kwa maana nitainua mchungaji katika nchi ambaye hatawajali wanaoangamia, wala hatawatafuta wachanga, wala hatawaponya waliojeruhiwa, wala hatawalisha walio wazima, bali atakula nyama ya kondoo walionona na kuzirarua kwato zao."
sw.R: Nitaipa nchi mchungaji ambaye hatawajali kondoo wanaokufa. Hatawatafuta wachanga wala hatawaponya walioumia. Hatawalisha walio wazima. Badala yake, atakula nyama ya kondoo walionona na hata kuzirarua kwato zao."

vi.L: Vì kìa, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dấy lên một người chăn trong xứ; con đang chết nó sẽ không chăm sóc, con non nó sẽ không tìm kiếm, con bị thương nó sẽ không chữa lành, con khỏe mạnh nó sẽ không nuôi dưỡng; nhưng thịt con béo nó sẽ ăn, và móng của chúng nó sẽ xé ra."
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp dấy lên trong xứ một người chăn không chăm sóc những con đang chết, không tìm kiếm những con non, không chữa lành những con bị thương, không nuôi những con khỏe mạnh, nhưng ăn thịt những con béo và xé cả móng của chúng."
vi.R: Ta sẽ ban cho xứ một người chăn chẳng lo gì đến những con chiên đang chết. Nó sẽ không tìm kiếm những con non, cũng không chữa lành những con bị thương. Nó sẽ không cho những con khỏe mạnh ăn. Trái lại, nó sẽ ăn thịt những con chiên béo và xé cả móng của chúng."

ko.L: 보아라, 내가 이 땅에 한 목자를 세우겠다. 그는 망해 가는 것들을 돌보지 않고, 어린 것을 찾지 않으며, 상한 것을 고치지 않고, 성한 것을 먹이지 않으며, 살진 것들의 고기를 먹고 그 발굽을 찢을 것이다."
ko.B: 내가 이 땅에 한 목자를 세우겠다. 그는 죽어 가는 양들을 돌보지 않고, 어린 양들을 찾지 않으며, 다친 양들을 고치지 않고, 성한 양들을 먹이지 않을 것이다. 도리어 살진 양들의 고기를 먹고 그 발굽까지 뜯어낼 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 이 땅에 한 목자를 줄 것이다. 그는 죽어 가는 양들을 돌보지 않을 것이다. 어린 양들을 찾지도 않고, 다친 양들을 고쳐 주지도 않을 것이다. 성한 양들을 먹이지도 않을 것이다. 오히려 살진 양들의 고기를 먹고 그 발굽까지 뜯어낼 것이다."

decisions.choice: a shepherd who will not care for the perishing: the bad shepherds of Ezekiel 34
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 34:2-4 charges the shepherds of Israel with the same failures: they did not strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind up the injured or seek the lost, but ate the fat and clothed themselves with the wool. This shepherd is the LORD's judgment on a flock that rejected the good shepherd (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the young: the young of the flock
decisions.reason: The word usually means a youth. Some read it as "the scattered" or "the straying", from a similar word, which would fit Ezekiel 34:4, "the lost you have not sought". The sense of the list is the same: the shepherd neglects every sheep that needs him.

decisions.choice: eat the meat of the fat and tear off their hooves: greed that leaves nothing
decisions.reason: The shepherd eats the best of the flock, and even tears the hooves apart for the last scraps of meat, or by driving the sheep without care. He lives off the flock instead of caring for it.

decisions.choice: who will not care for ... (B); He will not ... (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts each sheep first, for emphasis: "the perishing he will not care for". Literal keeps that order; Balanced and Readable use the order English expects. The LORD's words end here.

decisions.choice: "nó" for the foolish shepherd
decisions.reason: The shepherd raised up as a judgment is a guilty figure, so Vietnamese speaks of him with "nó", as it does of the guilty in the oracles.

source.text: ה֣וֹי רֹעִ֤י הָֽאֱלִיל֙ עֹזְבִ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן חֶ֥רֶב עַל־זְרוֹע֖וֹ וְעַל־עֵ֣ין יְמִינ֑וֹ זְרֹעוֹ֙ יָב֣וֹשׁ תִּיבָ֔שׁ וְעֵ֥ין יְמִינ֖וֹ כָּהֹ֥ה תִכְהֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to] the shepherd of worthlessness, abandoning the flock! A sword [be] on his arm and on his right eye! His arm will wither completely, and his right eye will grow completely dim.

en.L: Woe, worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! \q A sword on his arm and on his right eye! \q His arm will wither completely, \q and his right eye will grow completely dim.
en.B: Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! \q May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! \q Let his arm wither away, \q and his right eye go completely blind!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the worthless shepherd who deserts the sheep! \q A sword will strike his arm and his right eye. \q His arm will become completely useless, \q and his right eye will become totally blind.

es.L: ¡Ay del pastor inútil, que abandona el rebaño! \q ¡Espada sobre su brazo y sobre su ojo derecho! \q Su brazo se secará del todo, \q y su ojo derecho se oscurecerá por completo.
es.B: ¡Ay del pastor inútil que abandona el rebaño! \q ¡Que la espada hiera su brazo y su ojo derecho! \q ¡Que su brazo se seque del todo, \q y su ojo derecho quede ciego por completo!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el pastor que no vale nada y abandona a las ovejas! \q Una espada herirá su brazo y su ojo derecho. \q Su brazo quedará completamente inútil, \q y su ojo derecho quedará totalmente ciego.

fr.L: Malheur, berger de néant, qui abandonne le troupeau ! \q L’épée sur son bras et sur son œil droit ! \q Son bras se desséchera complètement, \q et son œil droit s’obscurcira complètement.
fr.B: Malheur au berger de rien qui abandonne le troupeau ! \q Que l’épée frappe son bras et son œil droit ! \q Que son bras se dessèche entièrement \q et que son œil droit devienne tout à fait aveugle !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour le berger bon à rien qui abandonne les moutons ! \q Une épée frappera son bras et son œil droit. \q Son bras ne pourra plus du tout servir, \q et son œil droit deviendra complètement aveugle.

sw.L: Ole, mchungaji asiyefaa kitu, aliachaye kundi! \q Upanga juu ya mkono wake na juu ya jicho lake la kuume! \q Mkono wake utakauka kabisa, \q na jicho lake la kuume litafifia kabisa.
sw.B: Ole wake mchungaji asiyefaa kitu, aliyeliacha kundi! \q Upanga na upige mkono wake na jicho lake la kuume! \q Mkono wake na ukauke kabisa, \q na jicho lake la kuume lipofuke kabisa!
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa mchungaji asiyefaa kitu anayewaacha kondoo! \q Upanga utaupiga mkono wake na jicho lake la kuume. \q Mkono wake hautafaa kitu kabisa, \q na jicho lake la kuume litapofuka kabisa.

vi.L: Khốn cho kẻ chăn vô dụng, là kẻ bỏ bầy! \q Gươm ở trên cánh tay nó và trên mắt phải nó! \q Cánh tay nó sẽ khô héo hoàn toàn, \q và mắt phải nó sẽ mờ tối hoàn toàn.
vi.B: Khốn cho kẻ chăn vô dụng bỏ mặc bầy chiên! \q Nguyện gươm đánh vào cánh tay và mắt phải nó! \q Nguyện cánh tay nó khô héo hẳn, \q và mắt phải nó mù hẳn!
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho kẻ chăn vô dụng bỏ mặc bầy chiên! \q Gươm sẽ đánh vào cánh tay và mắt phải của nó. \q Cánh tay nó sẽ hoàn toàn vô dụng, \q và mắt phải nó sẽ mù hẳn.

ko.L: 양 떼를 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 화가 있다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 그의 오른쪽 눈 위에! \q 그의 팔이 아주 말라 버리고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈이 아주 어두워질 것이다.
ko.B: 양 떼를 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 화가 있다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 오른쪽 눈을 치기를! \q 그의 팔이 아주 말라 버리고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈이 아주 멀어 버리기를!
ko.R: 양들을 버리는 쓸모없는 목자에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! \q 칼이 그의 팔과 오른쪽 눈을 칠 것이다. \q 그의 팔은 전혀 쓸 수 없게 되고, \q 그의 오른쪽 눈은 완전히 멀 것이다.

decisions.choice: the worthless shepherd: a shepherd of no worth, like an idol
decisions.reason: The word for "worthless" means "nothingness", and it is a common word for idols, the "worthless gods" (Leviticus 19:4; Isaiah 2:8). The shepherd who abandons the flock is as useless as an idol.

decisions.choice: a sword on his arm and on his right eye: judgment on his strength and his sight
decisions.reason: The arm is a shepherd's strength to protect the flock, and the eye his watchfulness. He used neither for the sheep, and he will lose both. The right side was the stronger and more valued side.

decisions.choice: woe ... the sword ... will wither: a curse that is also a prediction
alternatives: a sword will strike his arm (as a statement)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb in the line about the sword, which may be read as a wish ("may the sword strike") or as a statement ("the sword will strike"). The last lines are statements about what will happen. The poem returns to the shepherd in 13:7-9, where the LORD calls for the sword against his shepherd.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The cry *hoy* follows the wording set in Isaiah. Balanced reads the sword line as a wish, Readable as a statement; Literal keeps the Hebrew without a verb (m3).

decisions.choice: "berger de néant" (L); "berger de rien" (B); "bon à rien" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "nothingness", a word for idols (meaning decision m1); "néant" keeps that at Literal.
